marketing.metaTitle: Pickld: eight moments, one real day
marketing.metaDescription: Pickld is a photo diary for the day you actually had. Fill a jar with eight moments, decorate them with stickers and let your friends read along. Coming soon to iPhone.

hero.body: Pickld is a photo diary for the day you actually had. Fill a jar with eight photos, from where you are to how your evening went, then let your friends read it.
hero.jarAlt: Joff’s Sunday on Pickld: a jar of photos, each labelled with its moment, like #whereami and #ootd, with 15 likes and 10 comments

form.label: Email address
form.note: We’ll email you a 6-digit code to check it’s you, then only about Pickld’s launch.

moments.title: One jar a day. Eight moments to fill.
moments.body: Every moment has its own slot, so your jar tells the whole day, not just the highlight. Each slot is a small prompt, not a rule: fill it with whatever your day actually looked like. A new jar starts at midnight.
moments.label: The eight moments
moments.outro: Fill as many as you like. A half-full jar is still a real day.

whereami.title: Where you are right now
whereami.question: Where are you right now?
whereami.body: The place you’re in, big or small. Trips count, but so do the ordinary spots your day passes through.
whereami.e1: The jeepney window on the way to work
whereami.e2: Your desk, coffee ring and all
whereami.e3: The new café you finally tried
whereami.e5: The beach you saved up for
whereami.long: Snap the place you’re in, whatever it is. A new city counts, and so does the jeepney window, the waiting room or the corner of your room you never leave. Months later, these are the photos that tell you where your days actually went.
whereami.e6: A waiting room, number in hand
whereami.e7: The view from your bedroom window
whereami.e8: A street you’ve never walked before

mebusywith.title: What’s keeping you busy
mebusywith.question: What’s keeping you busy?
mebusywith.body: Whatever has your hands or your head today: work, school, a hobby, or resting on purpose.
mebusywith.e3: Packing orders for your side hustle
mebusywith.e5: A mountain of laundry to fold
mebusywith.long: Whatever has your hands or your head today. Work and school count, and so do the small jobs nobody sees: cooking, caring for someone, fixing something, or finally resting because you needed it.
mebusywith.e6: Dinner prep for the whole family

whoamiwith.title: Who you’re with
whoamiwith.question: Who are you with?
whoamiwith.body: Your company today. It doesn’t have to be a person: a pet, a plant, a good book, or just you all count.
whoamiwith.e1: Your barkada at the merienda spot
whoamiwith.e2: Your dog, waiting by the door
whoamiwith.e3: The plant you’ve kept alive all year
whoamiwith.e4: A book you can’t put down
whoamiwith.long: Your company today, whoever or whatever it is. It doesn’t have to be a person: a pet, a plant, a good book, a show you’re hooked on, or just you. Quiet days alone count as much as loud days with the barkada.
whoamiwith.e7: Your cat, sitting on your keyboard
whoamiwith.e8: The coworker who saved your day

ootd.title: Today’s outfit
ootd.question: What are you wearing today?
ootd.body: What you actually wore, not what you’d post. Pambahay counts.
ootd.e3: The office fit you planned last night
ootd.e4: Gym clothes that never saw the gym
ootd.long: What you actually wore today, not what you’d dress up for a post. Pambahay, uniform, work clothes or the shirt you slept in all count. Look back in a year and you’ll see your real wardrobe, and your real life.
ootd.e6: Rain boots and a borrowed jacket
ootd.e7: Matching shirts at a family party

selfie.title: Your face, as it is
selfie.question: How are you feeling?
selfie.body: How you look and feel right now. Pickld has no beauty filters or retouching, so it’s really you.
selfie.e1: Sleepy, first thing in the morning
selfie.e5: Tired but happy on the ride home
selfie.long: How you look and feel right now: sleepy, proud, sweaty or glowing. Pickld has color filters but no beauty filters or face retouching, so it’s really you. Not feeling it? Any photo of you counts, even your shadow.

morning.title: How the day began
morning.question: How’s your morning going?
morning.body: The first part of your day, however it started: early, late or somewhere in between.
morning.e5: The alarm you snoozed three times
morning.long: The first stretch of your day, however it started. Early run or late alarm, pandesal or no breakfast at all. The Now tile points to #morning from 5 in the morning until noon.
morning.e6: The light coming through your window

afternoon.title: The middle of it all
afternoon.question: How’s your afternoon going?
afternoon.body: The stretch between lunch and going home: the busy part, the slump and the snack that saves it.
afternoon.long: The middle of it all, from lunch until you head home. It’s the busy part, the slump and the merienda that saves it. Afternoons are the part of the day we forget fastest, so they’re worth a photo.
afternoon.e6: Merienda: turon and a cold drink
afternoon.e7: Your shoes up on a desk
afternoon.e8: The long line at the bank

evening.title: How it ended
evening.question: How was your day?
evening.body: The way your day wound down, quiet or not.
evening.e4: A late game night with friends
evening.long: How your day wound down, quiet or not. Dinner, the commute home, a night out or your bed at last. An evening moment closes the jar, so it’s the one you’ll see first when you look back.
evening.e6: The commute home through city lights

moments.metaDescription: What goes in each of Pickld’s eight daily moments, from #whereami to #evening, with ideas for each. #whoamiwith doesn’t have to be a person.

how.title: Snap. Decorate. Share.
how.snapBody: Take the photo and it drops into the right slot. No signal? It’s saved on your phone and uploads later.
how.snapAlt: Today on Pickld: 6 of 8 moments in today’s jar, each photo with its time and #tag, with #selfie and #evening still open to fill
how.decorateBody: Color filters, stickers, speech bubbles and text. No beauty filters or face retouching, ever.
how.decorateAlt: Pickld’s photo editor on an #afternoon photo, with tabs for Filters, Stickers, Bubble and Text and a row of color filters
how.shareBody: Publish your jar for the people who read you, or turn a moment or the whole jar into a card for your Stories, with your pickld.me link on it.
how.shareAlt: Share jar on Pickld: a card of Dale’s Thursday with all eight photos and his pickld.me link, with buttons to save the image, copy the link or share it
how.body: Three steps, all in the app, from the moment it happens to your friends reading it.

snapPoints.p1: The Now tile picks the moment for the time of day: morning, afternoon or evening.
snapPoints.p2: Choose from your gallery and the photo joins the day it was taken.
snapPoints.p3: Missed one? Fill in any past day later; it shows a small “Added later” badge.
snapPoints.p4: Offline, it’s saved on your phone and uploads when you’re back.

decoratePoints.p1: 16 color filters, named for Pinoy days, like Kalamansi, Kape and Halo-halo.
decoratePoints.p2: Stickers from free packs, Olivia’s pack and very Pinoy packs.
decoratePoints.p3: Speech, thought, shout and whisper bubbles, and text in 8 fonts.
decoratePoints.p4: No beauty filters or face retouching, ever.

sharePoints.p1: Publish the jar for your readers, for everyone, or only you.
sharePoints.p2: Turn a moment or the whole jar into a card for your Stories, in 9:16 or 4:5.
sharePoints.p3: Pick from layouts, from one big photo to a grid of eight.
sharePoints.p4: Every card carries your pickld.me link so friends can find you.

stickers.title: Meet Olivia
stickers.body: Olivia is a real cat: white, fluffy and not impressed. She has her own sticker pack, next to free packs for every moment and packs made for very Pinoy days.
stickers.packAlt: Olivia’s pack on Pickld: a white cat with a crown, hearts and a sleepy face, 16 stickers for ₱49

privacy.title: Yours, on your terms
privacy.body: Every jar picks its own audience when you publish it.
privacy.readersBody: The people you let read you. This is the default.
privacy.everyoneBody: Anyone with the link, and your page at pickld.me.
privacy.onlyMeBody: Keep this jar just for you.
privacy.controlsTitle: You decide who you see, and who sees you

private.title: Private moments
private.body: Mark one moment private and it stays with you: never in feeds, share cards, notifications or our analytics.

location.title: No location in your photos
location.body: Pickld removes location data from your photos before they upload. Only the time is kept.

mute.title: Mute without drama
mute.body: Mute someone you read and their posts leave your Moments and Jars. You stay their reader, and they aren’t told.

block.title: Block anyone
block.body: Blocked people can’t see your jars or find your profile, and they aren’t told.

discover.title: Stay out of Discover
discover.body: Turn off Show me in Discover to stay out of Discover and suggestions.

teens.title: Safer for teens
teens.body: Under 18, your posts stay out of Discover and suggestions.

memories.title: Look back without scrolling
memories.body: On this day brings back your jar from a year ago, monthly recaps add up your moments, and a home screen widget keeps today’s jar one tap away.
memories.memoriesAlt: Memories on Pickld: a jar from one year ago and an October recap
memories.widgetAlt: The Pickld widget on an iPhone home screen: 4 of 8 moments today, next up #whoamiwith

faq.title: Questions
faq.freeA: Yes. Jars, readers and the free sticker packs cost nothing. Some extra sticker packs will cost a little, and what you buy is yours to keep.
faq.androidA: Pickld starts on iPhone. Android comes later; join the waitlist and we’ll tell you when it’s ready.
faq.androidASoon: Pickld starts on iPhone. Android comes later.
faq.whoA: Your readers, unless you choose otherwise. Make a jar Everyone to share it with a link, or Only me to keep it to yourself. You can block anyone.
faq.fullQ: Do I have to fill all eight?
faq.fullA: No. A jar holds up to eight moments, and messy, half-full days count too.
faq.missedQ: What if I miss a moment?
faq.missedA: Fill it in later. Any past day can be filled, and those moments get a small “Added later” badge so your readers know.
faq.ageQ: How old do I need to be?
faq.label: Frequently asked questions

story.metaDescription: We started Pickld more than ten years ago, set it aside for healthcare technology, and promised to come back. This is that promise, kept.
story.lead: Pickld isn’t new. We started it more than ten years ago, put it down for something bigger, and promised ourselves we’d return one day. This is that day.
story.quote: “The easiest way to tell your story.”
story.quoteBy: The first Pickld’s line, more than ten years ago

first.title: The first Pickld
first.body: We built the first Pickld, right here on pickld.me, around one idea: eight moments make one real day. It was the easiest way to tell your story, your days as they really were, not as they were supposed to look.

calling.title: A bigger calling
calling.body: Healthcare technology called, and we answered. Helping people get better care mattered more than a photo app, so we set Pickld aside and gave those years to it.

promise.title: A promise
promise.body: We never really let go. We swore to each other that one day, we’d get back to Pickld.

now.title: Pickld, again
now.body: Pickld is back, and the eight moments are still its heart. What’s new is everything around them, made for how we share today: jars your friends actually read, stickers, and cards for your Stories. Starting in the Philippines, on iPhone first.

story.videoBody: “You Deserve to Be You!”, one of the first Pickld videos, made in January 2016.

story.finalBody: That was true ten years ago, and it’s still why we make Pickld. Join the waitlist to be among the first to fill a jar.
story.finalBodySoon: That was true ten years ago, and it’s still why we make Pickld. It’s coming soon to iPhone.

why.metaDescription: More than ten years ago, Pickld started as a simple way to keep your days and be yourself. It still shows the people you choose, newest first, and likes never decide what you see.
why.lead: We started Pickld more than ten years ago as a simple way to keep the moments of your day and be yourself while doing it. Since then, most social apps have learned to decide what you see by what keeps you scrolling. Pickld didn’t. You see the people you choose, newest first, and you meet new people through the ones you already know.
why.promise: “Your feed is for the people you choose. Discover is for the people you haven’t met yet.”
why.harmTitle: What engagement algorithms do to us
why.harmBody: Most feeds are ranked to keep you hooked. You pay with your time, your attention and sometimes what you believe. This is what the evidence shows.

design.title: Built to keep you scrolling
design.body: Platforms are often designed to maximize engagement, with infinite scroll, like counts and algorithms that use your data to choose what you see.

beliefs.title: They can change what you believe
beliefs.body: Seven weeks on X’s algorithmic feed shifted users’ political opinions and the accounts they followed. Switching the algorithm off afterwards didn’t undo it.

voices.title: They choose whose voice is heard
voices.body: The same study found X’s algorithm promoted conservative political content and pushed down posts from traditional news media.

time.title: They take your time
time.body: When people were moved off Facebook’s and Instagram’s ranking algorithms onto a newest-first feed, the time they spent on the apps dropped substantially.

kids.title: Kids pay the most
kids.body: Up to 95% of teens use social media, and more than a third say they’re on it almost constantly. Teens on it more than 3 hours a day faced double the risk of depression and anxiety symptoms.

law.title: Lawmakers are stepping in
law.body: The EU now requires the largest platforms to explain their recommendation systems and to offer at least one feed that isn’t based on profiling you.
law.source: EU Digital Services Act, Articles 27 and 38

why.howTitle: How Pickld decides what you see
why.howBody: Every list follows a rule you can read. None of them uses likes, comments or reader counts.

moments.title: Moments
moments.body: Every moment from the people you read, newest first, by when it went up.

jars.title: Jars
jars.body: Your people’s days, one jar each. A jar moves to the top when someone adds a moment to it. Nothing else moves it.

discover.title: Discover
discover.body: Public posts from people you don’t read yet. People your authors read come first, each marked “Read by @name”. Then everyone else who posts publicly, newest first.

not.likes: Likes never move a post up, and nobody is ranked by how popular they are.
not.strangers: Nobody you didn’t choose is slipped into your Moments or Jars.
not.filters: No beauty or face-retouch filters. Color filters only.
not.private: Private moments stay with you: never in feeds, shared links or notifications.
not.analytics: No photos or captions go into our analytics.
not.claim: We don’t claim to be “algorithm-free”. Search, spam checks and safety reviews use algorithms. What we refuse is ranking your social life by engagement.

control.read: Read or stop reading anyone, any time.
control.mute: Mute someone you read. You stay their reader, their posts leave your timelines, and they aren’t told.
control.block: Block anyone. Neither of you sees the other.
control.discover: Turn off Show me in Discover to stay out of Discover and suggestions.
control.teens: Under 18, your posts stay out of Discover and suggestions.

why.researchBody: Every claim on this page comes from these. They don’t prove Pickld is better for you, and we don’t claim they do.

nature.title: The political effects of X’s feed algorithm
nature.source: Nature, 2026 · Gauthier, Hodler, Widmer and Zhuravskaya
nature.summary: In a seven-week field experiment with US users of X in 2023, switching from a chronological to an algorithmic feed increased engagement and shifted some political opinions.
nature.limit: Switching from algorithmic back to chronological had no comparable effect. One platform, one period.

science.title: How do social media feed algorithms affect attitudes and behavior in an election campaign?
science.source: Science, 2023 · Guess, Malhotra, Pan, Barberá and colleagues
science.summary: During the 2020 US election, people moved to reverse-chronological Facebook and Instagram feeds spent less time on the platforms and saw different content.
science.limit: The chronological feed did not significantly change the polarization or political attitudes the study measured.

surgeon.title: Social Media and Youth Mental Health
surgeon.summary: Finds that platforms are often designed to maximize engagement, including with recommendation algorithms, and that heavy use is linked to a higher risk of poor mental health in teens.
surgeon.limit: The advisory says more research is needed, and that social media can also benefit some young people.

dsa.title: Digital Services Act, Articles 27 and 38
dsa.summary: Platforms must explain the main parameters of their recommender systems. The largest must offer at least one option not based on profiling.
dsa.limit: It’s a law, not a study, and Pickld is not one of the very large platforms it targets.

why.finalBody: More than ten years on, it’s still a simple way to keep your days and be yourself. Pickld is coming to iPhone; join the waitlist to be among the first to fill a jar.
why.finalBodySoon: More than ten years on, it’s still a simple way to keep your days and be yourself. Pickld is coming soon to iPhone.

mission.metaDescription: More than ten years ago, we wanted a simple way to keep our moments and be ourselves. That’s still Pickld’s mission, and these are the rules it holds itself to.
mission.lead: More than ten years ago, we wanted one simple thing: a way to keep the moments of a day and be ourselves at the same time. That was the first Pickld, and it’s still the mission. Social media should help people connect, not compete for their attention.
mission.quote: “The easiest way to tell your story.”
mission.quoteBy: The first Pickld’s line, more than ten years ago
mission.originBody: The first Pickld was eight moments that make one real day: where you were, who you were with, how the day began and how it ended. Your days as they really were, not as they were supposed to look, and you in them. Pickld is back with the same idea at its heart.

people.title: People over engagement
people.body: Feeds built to maximize engagement hold people’s time and can even shift what they believe. More time in the app isn’t our goal. A good day on Pickld is a jar of your day and a look at your friends’ days.

choice.title: Your choice, not our guess
choice.body: Who you read decides what you see. We don’t predict what will keep you hooked.

open.title: Rules you can read
open.body: Every list follows a plain rule, explained in the app and on this site. When we change one, we’ll say so.

calm.title: Calm by default
calm.body: No streaks, no countdowns, no guilt. The only reminders are the ones you set.

safe.title: Safety, not attention
safe.body: Moderation removes what breaks our community guidelines. It never boosts or buries posts to win attention.

private.title: Private by design
private.body: Private moments never leave you. Location stays out of your photos, and photos and captions stay out of our analytics.

mission.promise: Follow who matters. See what they share. Discover who connects you.
mission.finalTitle: Fill a jar with your day.
mission.finalBody: Pickld is coming to iPhone. Join the waitlist to be among the first to try it.
mission.finalBodySoon: Pickld is coming soon to iPhone.

features.metaDescription: Close friends, calm controls, a Lock Screen widget and more: a look at what’s new in Pickld, the photo diary for the day you actually had.
features.lead: Pickld keeps getting better at one thing: keeping up with the people you care about, without asking for more of your time. Here are a few of our newest features.
features.heroAlt: Today on Pickld: eight 3:4 tiles for the day’s moments, from #whereami to #evening

close.title: Close friends
close.body: Some days are just for your inner circle. Pick Close friends when you publish, and only the people on your list see it.
close.p1: Choose your list from the people who read you.
close.p2: Everyone else can’t tell those moments exist.
close.p3: Nobody is told when you add or remove them.
close.alt: Close friends on Pickld: a list of your readers with a switch for each, and 2 people on the list

calm.title: Calm controls
calm.body: Pickld is calm by default, and now you can make it quieter still.
calm.p1: Hide like counts: no like numbers on posts, yours included. You can still like things.
calm.p2: Take a break: pause your reminders and pushes for up to two weeks.
calm.p3: Everything waits in Notifications, and nobody is told you’re away.
calm.alt: Calm settings on Pickld: Hide like counts and Take a break, under Quiet hours

features.moreBody: Small things that make a big difference to how Pickld feels.

private.title: Approve who reads you
private.body: Make your account private and you approve each new reader. Accounts under 18 always do.

widget.title: Lock Screen and StandBy
widget.body: See today’s jar at a glance: how many moments you’ve added and which one is next.

describe.title: Photo descriptions
describe.body: Add a short description to a photo, and VoiceOver reads it to everyone who can see the moment.

mention.title: Tag your people
mention.body: Add a mention sticker to tag someone. You can tag people who read each other with you.

place.title: Place stickers
place.body: Say where you are in your own words. Pickld keeps only the words, never your exact location.

straighten.title: Straighten
straighten.body: A fine tilt dial in Crop levels a crooked horizon in a second.

features.saving: There’s more we’re saving for launch day.
features.finalBody: Pickld is coming to iPhone. Join the waitlist to be among the first to try it.
features.finalBodySoon: Pickld is coming soon to iPhone.
